verdicts.summary: No Lean counterpart was found. (1.2) is the incompressible Euler system, introducing the notation D_t u for the material acceleration. No declaration was found in the audited NavierStokes/ tree that states it: the whole tree never mentions Euler (a grep for `Euler` over NavierStokes/ returns zero hits, EuclideanSpace is spelled otherwise), and it has no named material-derivative operator ∂_t + (u·∇) — the `material` names it does carry (NavierStokes.PhaseCalculus.signedMaterialOp, PhaseCalculus.lean:139, and the PrimaryMaterialDefect/ActualPhaseDefect families) are phase-transport operators ∂_V + σε∂_T + b∂_R + (V/R)∂_θ + εG∂_Z in slot coordinates, not this system. The pieces of (1.2) are all present as separate definitions — temporalDerivative (∂_t u, ProblemStatement.lean:55), advection ((u·∇)u, line 63), pressureGradient (∇p, line 71), spatialDivergence (∇·u, line 67) — and the Lean states only the viscous equation (1.1): `navierStokesResidual ν u p t x = f (t,x)` with residual ∂_t u + (u·∇)u − ν•Δu + ∇p, imposed in CandidateProperties.navier_stokes (R3/ProblemStatement.lean:106) together with divergence_free (line 104). Substituting ν := 0 there would reproduce (1.2) verbatim, signs included (residual = f ⟺ D_t u = −∇p + f), but no declaration performs that substitution and every statement in the development carries ν > 0 (Theorem 1.1 quantifies over ν > 0); a grep for `navierStokesResidual 0` over NavierStokes/ returns nothing. The closest formula in the repository is Euler/EulerProof.lean:10738, `momentumResidual u p z = fderiv ℝ u z (1, u z) + gradient p`, whose first term is exactly D_t u (the spacetime derivative applied to (1, u)); it is the UNFORCED residual (no f), carries no incompressibility constraint, and lies in the Euler half of the repository, which is outside this audit's scope. Severity low: (1.2) is expository — it appears in §1.1 'Historical context and previous work', the notation D_t occurs nowhere else in the 166 pages (searched the text layer for 'Dt': two hits, both on this page), and no later step of the paper uses it.
